text:
Zoe M.: hey all 44b day 1 here. quick practical question: what's the compact rule for where to post stuff so i don't clog channels? eg: laptop/badge requests, expense receipts, time-off, PR review pings, CI alerts, and social/lunch. also how do i mute bots but still get things that mention me?

Ravi (IT): welcome Zoe! short map: #help = hardware/accounts/badge; #finance = expenses (use the expense app, don't paste receipts in threads); #people-ops = PTO & onboarding questions; #eng-code-reviews = cross-team PR visibility; #ci-notifications or #eng-releases = build/deploy events. social=> #random or #lunch-plans.

Jenna PeopleOps: add: use the PTO app for formal requests so managers can approve and it's tracked. For vendor/office pickups ping #people-ops with vendor name and ETA.

Marco Eng: PR etiquette: post the PR link in the PR itself. If you need cross-team visibility, one short message in #eng-code-reviews with the link is fine. Avoid pasting logs; use a gist or artifact link. Reactions are our cheap ACKs (:eyes:, :white_check_mark:).

Zoe M.: bots 914 i get daily standup and ci pings. i want to hide them but still get mentions/keywords.

Ravi (IT): channel-level: channel > Preferences > Notification preferences: set "All new messages" off, turn on "Direct messages, mentions & keywords" and "Replies to threads you're in." Add keywords like your full name or team name so you only get alerts for them.

Ravi (IT): bot-level: many bots support opt-in or config. For example, infra-bot can be set to post only failures to #eng and successes to #ci-notifications. ping @IT or post in #eng-infra and we can move or reconfigure webhooks.

infra-bot: CI status: build=main success (posted to #ci-notifications)

Marco Eng: other etiquette:
- use threads for follow-ups to keep channels searchable
- use reactions instead of "thanks" replies
- avoid @channel unless it's an actual org-wide urgent note
- for long debugging logs, paste to a gist and link it

Jenna PeopleOps: pro tips: pin the onboarding checklist in #new-hires and react to the welcome message to opt into the onboarding flow. Also set your Slack timezone and working hours (Profile > Preferences > Notifications > Do Not Disturb) so teammates know when youre reachable.

Zoe M.: what's the policy on creating new channels?

Marco Eng: create a new channel if more than ~3 people need ongoing coordination or if it's a distinct topic that would spam others. Make it private if it's just a small pod. Add a short channel purpose and pin key docs.

Ravi (IT): if a bot is spamming everyone, ask us to move it to a dedicated channel. We can also set message filters so only failures or high-severity alerts go to main channels.

Zoe M.: neat. any tips about using reactions/ack patterns?

Marco Eng: common patterns: :eyes: = seen; :white_check_mark: = done; :hourglass_flowing_sand: = in progress. Use threads for status updates so the root message isn't flooded.

onboard-bot: Onboarding checklist update: account created, 2FA pending, laptop request submitted, manager intro scheduled (see /onboarding).

Zoe M.: thanks all! i'll submit badge in #help, expense in #finance, lunch poll in #random and join #new-hires. also following up with IT to quiet infra-bot unless it fails. :raised_hands:
